audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2 and 2+ items are given to Swain, and Level 6 to 'Skill', but the packet chart reads Skill/Skill/Swain/Skill/Swain/Swain/Skill. The whys agree with the packet, not the chart: whys[1] describes the clone eating your E, whys[4] describes Demonic Ascension out-sustaining Cyclone, and whys[6] says the late game 'stays even'.
audit.why: Three rows disagreed with their own explanations at a 50.64% win rate over 314 games.
audit.corrected: Row 1 to Skill, row 4 to Swain (7/10), row 6 to Skill; win[] and phases[].side proposed as pairs.

audit.why: Four spikes present and coherent: Level 3 root pattern, Level 6 Demonic Ascension into Cyclone, first item poke, and Wukong's own Levels 1-2 burst window. No fabricated timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing tells you what Wukong's commit looks like at the frame level. Crushing Blow (Q) is an auto-attack reset, so the tell is the attack wind-up, not the ability cast. The Don't slot about his Q carried only generic filler.
audit.why: Flagged in missingInteractions for this matchup. With a clone in the lane, reading the real body one beat earlier is the difference between rooting him and rooting air. Swain's Nevermove is 12 s at rank 1 — an E spent on the decoy is 12 seconds of no setup.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d now gives the reset tell; phases[1].why gives Nevermove's rank-1 cooldown and ties it to not spending E on the clone.

audit.why: The clone-baits-your-E interaction is already the spine of this page and is stated in whys[1], early, late, wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0]. Nothing further asserted, since the brief carries no Wukong kit file.

edits.before: E-root into the pull is your whole kill setup. Only take the trade when Wukong's Nimbus Strike is down.
edits.after: Nevermove is your whole setup, down 12 s at rank 1 — never spend it on the clone, only on the real body.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Crushing Blow resets his auto — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast.

notes: The brief carries enemyKit: null for Wukong, so no Riot cooldowns or ability text were available on his side — no numbers were asserted for any Wukong ability, and the existing armour-shred claims were left untouched rather than restated without a source.
